post.description: The first factor of a local break-glass account (ADM-142). Success answers 204 and sets exactly one cookie, the pending-sign-in cookie (__Host-adiq_pending: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, at most 5 minutes). The response carries no session, no token and no body. The cookie authorises nothing except the second-factor operations. Every failure has one shape, 401 /problems/sign-in-failed: unknown account, wrong password, non-local account, disabled account and throttled account are indistinguishable by status, body, headers and timing class (an unknown account still costs one password verification). A throttled account is delayed on the server, never locked (rule 3). The source-IP limiter may answer 429 with Retry-After, which does not depend on the account named. Refused on any hostname bound to AN-5 or AN-7, and outside the console source-CIDR allow-list, with the same 401.

204.description: The password step passed. Only the pending-sign-in cookie is set.

Set-Cookie.description: The pending-sign-in cookie, __Host-adiq_pending, and no other cookie.

get.description: Returns the value the console sends in the X-CSRF-Token header on every mutation. It is bound to the session, readable only with that session cookie, and not a credential: it authorises nothing alone.

Needs the pending-sign-in cookie. Success and failure behave as for verifyWebAuthnSignIn.

post.description: Needs the pending-sign-in cookie from a first factor. Answers the WebAuthn request options for the account's enrolled credentials. A missing, expired, consumed or exhausted pending sign-in gets 401 /problems/sign-in-failed, the same as a wrong factor.

post.description: Needs the pending-sign-in cookie. On success the pending sign-in is consumed, a new session is created with a new ID, and the response (204, no body) sets the session cookie and clears the pending cookie. Any failure is 401 /problems/sign-in-failed and counts against the pending sign-in's five attempts.

get.description: The redirect URI of the attestation sign-in. No session or token is read: the single-use state issued by the start is the credential, and the tenant is the one the state names, used only to look the state up. A bad, expired or replayed state, a refused code, a token of another tenant and a failed read all answer the same 303 to the failed page, so the caller learns nothing about the cause (the cause is in the audit). Success answers 303 to the recorded page. The response carries no token and no directory value.

parameters.description: The state issued by the start.
parameters.name: state

parameters.description: The authorization code. Absent when the IdP reports an error.
parameters.name: code

parameters.description: The IdP error code, when the administrator declined or the IdP refused. Never echoed.
parameters.name: error

get.summary: Return from the IdP sign-in of a takeover-protection attestation (AN-11)

post.description: Starts the TM-D17 attestation of an Entra connection. The answer is the IdP sign-in URL (authorization code with PKCE, one delegated read-only scope, no offline access) at which a Global Administrator of that tenant signs in. The server then makes the one read of the tenant's sync features itself and discards the token. Needs a fresh step-up.

200.description: The sign-in URL for the Global Administrator

put.description: Sets attestation_max_age. A longer age widens the window in which a missed takeover-flag flip still counts as attested, so it needs the same permission and a fresh step-up as starting an attestation. The value is at most 90 days (7776000 seconds).
put.summary: Set how long an attestation stays valid
